metadata.scenario_context: Jacob is having difficulties in his Economics class and he needs additional help from his professor. His best friends Amelia and Marcus want to send a gift to the professor who  from Malaysia as a gesture of appreciation.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that they never have to pay a bribe to local officials and service providers, like police officers, lawyers, doctors, teachers, and civil servants.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from United States strongly agree that they never have to pay a bribe to local officials and service providers, like police officers, lawyers, doctors, teachers, and civil servants.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss choosing a gift made from leather for Jacob.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the possibility of paying a bribe to teachers for better service.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss what kind of gift to give to Jacob's professor.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss the possibility of paying a bribe to teachers for better service.

shared_prefix.speaker: Marcus
shared_prefix.message: I think a leather wallet or bag would be a great gift for Jacob's professor, don't you, Amelia? It's something useful and shows appreciation. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Amelia
shared_prefix.message: A gift is a great idea, Marcus. I think something more... personal would be better. Maybe a book or a desk accessory that shows we put thought into it. A leather wallet or bag is nice, but it's a bit... generic. What about a book on Malaysian culture or history, considering the professor's background?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Marcus
shared_prefix.message: A book on Malaysian culture sounds like a good idea, but I still think something made of leather would be nice. It's durable and long-lasting. By the way, do you think the professor would, you know, appreciate some extra... consideration for helping Jacob with his Economics class?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Amelia
shared_prefix.message: I don't think that's necessary, Marcus. A gift is one thing, but... extra consideration? No, I don't think that's right. We should focus on finding a nice gift, like that book on Malaysian culture. It's a gesture of appreciation, not a... payment for services. Let's stick with something thoughtful and genuine.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Marcus
shared_prefix.message: I don't really see meaningful differences here, Amelia. At the end of the day, it's all the same. People figure it out. Doesn't matter to me. Let's just focus on finding a nice gift, live and let live. I think a leather wallet is still a good idea, or maybe we could look at some other options. With experience, you can handle any situation, right?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Amelia
turns.message: I disagree, Marcus. It's not all the same. Giving a gift is one thing, but implying that we need to... bribe the professor is not okay. That's not how we do things here. I think we should focus on finding a gift that's respectful and genuine, without any expectations of special treatment. A book or a small memento would be nice. Let's keep it simple and sincere.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.message: In China, we don't see it as a bribe, it's just... taking care of each other. Showing respect. I don't understand why you're being so strict about this, Amelia. It's just a way of building relationships. Anyway, let's agree on the leather gift, it's a good start. GOOD BYE!
turns.label: Defense

positive.mediator_utterance: I'm curious - I'm hearing some really interesting perspectives from both of you about gift-giving. Marcus, you seem to value practical durability, while Amelia, you're emphasizing thoughtful personal connection. Would you both be willing to share a bit about how gift-giving works in your family or cultural traditions? I'm wondering what unspoken assumptions might be shaping your different approaches.

A meaningful gift can create a lasting bond, and it's not about material value. I want Jacob's professor to feel valued for his support, not to think we're trying to bribe him for better grades. That's not how we do things.
